answer.rationale: With the line at 94% of committed volume, no buffer, and only 14 days to expiry, switching primary vendor or deferring would raise delivery risk or lose continuity; adding a second source is valuable but cannot be stood up safely in this window. Renewing outright protects stability but forfeits the mandated 18% cut. Negotiating at renewal is the one move consistent with both constraints: memory_c1 supports incumbent continuity (no migration/interruption), memory_c6 supports term/volume leverage for unit-cost reduction, and memory_c4 is the load-bearing claim that benchmarking at renewal moved the incumbent on price and payment terms. I am verifying c4 before committing because the cost-cut case rests on it. Flagged risk: an aggressive 18% target could pressure service scope, quality, or allocation priority, so the ask should be framed around benchmarked price/payment terms and term length rather than narrowed service.
